themes.theme: ai and debt drive rates higher
themes.consensus_view: All three desks read the AI spending boom plus heavy government borrowing as forces that keep interest rates higher than the past decade, but they split on the long run: Allianz expects the same forces to pull long-term bond yields back down over ten years.

facts_agreed.claim: AI investment and government debt are raising the level of interest rates the economy settles at, and that shift is structural rather than temporary.
evidence_quotes: The structural factors pushing up r* are unlikely to subside.
interest rates are set to be higher-for-longer.

themes.consensus_view: Only one desk states a view here: Generali reads the Fed as having shifted to a tougher stance, raising rates and pointing to one more increase, and no other bank in this batch argues the other side.

themes.consensus_view: Only one desk stakes a directional view here: HSBC Asset Management says heavy, ongoing US government borrowing is pushing investors to demand more yield for holding long-dated Treasuries, with the 10-year already around 5 percent, and no other bank in the set argues the other side.

facts_agreed.claim: Continued heavy US government borrowing is making investors less willing to hold long-dated Treasuries without extra yield.
